subject: Dedicated cluster sizing: floor, burst lanes, and staged-commit options (Oxbridge Therapeutics)
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Gomez <aisha.gomez@oxbridge.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated cluster sizing: floor, burst lanes, and staged-commit options (Oxbridge Therapeutics)

Hi Aisha —

Thanks for the time yesterday. Per our conversation, attached are three concrete reservation options that balance cost predictability with the burst capacity you asked about. The attached workbook contains a short model (monthly burn forecast) and the assumptions behind the min-GPU floors. Summary here: 

Option 1 — Anchored Floor (lowest operational risk)
- Cluster baseline: 24 GPUs (reserved)
- Burst lanes: +12 GPUs available via warm-standby pool (pay-as-used)
- Ramp: 24 -> 36 over first 90 days; canonical canary window during weeks 3–4
- Warmup credits: 40 GPU-hours first 30 days
- Notes: best for steady inference throughput and strict SLOs

Option 2 — Staggered Onramp (cost smoothing)
- Cluster baseline: 12 GPUs (reserved)
- Burst lanes: +24 GPUs by shared burst pool (higher unit cost)
- Ramp: 12 -> 24 at month 3, optional step to 36 at month 6 based on usage triggers
- Commitment smoothing: monthly step increases to avoid high upfront spend

Option 3 — Pilot-to-Commit (phased escalation)
- Pilot: 8 GPUs reserved for 90 days with an irrevocable conversion window to a larger slate
- Post-pilot target: choose 24 or 36 GPUs depending on performance and KV cache hit-rate

A few clarifications we usually bake into these offers: minimum committed GPUs are counted against the reserved pool for billing; burst lanes may use lower-priority capacity with automatic fallbacks to open-hosted instances if a region is saturated. We can add a short SLA carve-out for the pilot phase if you need procurement sign-off.

Attached: oxbridge_dedicated_options_v2.xlsx (detailed cost model) and redwood-dedicated-terms-summary.pdf (term highlights including warmup credits, canary window, and DocuSign flow).

Next steps: if you can indicate a preferred option and target go-live quarter we’ll draft a term sheet and prepare a DocuSign envelope. Happy to run the cost model with your traffic sample if you send over 7 days of daytime traffic (token counts + average seq length).

Thanks,
Mina
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Aisha Gomez <aisha.gomez@oxbridge.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Caleb Ortiz <caleb.ortiz@oxbridge.ai>, Procurement <procurement@oxbridge.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated cluster sizing: floor, burst lanes, and staged-commit options (Oxbridge Therapeutics)

Mina —

Thanks for the clear options and workbook. A few clarifying questions from our side before we move to terms: 
1) For Option 1, is the +12 GPU warm-standby billed only when spun up, or is there a minimum monthly charge?
2) In Option 2, can we define explicit CPU/GPU burst windows (e.g., weekdays 09:00–18:00 PT) so our cost forecasting is accurate?
3) For the pilot in Option 3, will the KV cache be pre-warmed or do we need to run a separate warmup job?

Procurement also asked about termination language during the pilot and whether the pilot credits can be applied to the first committed month if we convert. We’ll also need a HubSpot link to attach to our internal case.

Appreciate it,
Aisha
Head of Platform Engineering
Oxbridge Therapeutics

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Gomez <aisha.gomez@oxbridge.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 13 Aug 2026 08:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated cluster sizing: floor, burst lanes, and staged-commit options (Oxbridge Therapeutics)

Hi Aisha —

Quick answers inline: 

> 1) For Option 1, is the +12 GPU warm-standby billed only when spun up, or is there a minimum monthly charge?
- The +12 warm-standby is billed on a usage basis when activated. There is a small idle reservation fee if you keep the pool pinned to your account (applies only if you reserve dedicated warm lanes); we made the model assume warm-standby is 100% on-demand to keep baseline predictable.

> 2) In Option 2, can we define explicit CPU/GPU burst windows (e.g., weekdays 09:00–18:00 PT) so our cost forecasting is accurate?
- Yes. We can codify burst windows and set them as policy-level rules. When a request hits outside those windows, fallback rules apply (either queue or scale up using a higher-cost pool). We’ll add a cost projection tab per window in the workbook.

> 3) For the pilot in Option 3, will the KV cache be pre-warmed or do we need to run a separate warmup job?
- We provide two approaches: (A) Redwood runs an automated pre-warm with a short golden prompt corpus (we charge the GPU-hours for the warmup but include a partial credit), or (B) you run your warmup script via our onboarding runbook (no charge from Redwood). For pilots that convert, we apply credited GPU-hours against the first committed invoice.

Procurement specifics: pilot termination is 30 days notice, standard pilot credits (40 GPU-hours) are applied pro-rata toward the first month after conversion. We’ll create a DocuSign term sheet with both pilot-conversion and step-up language.

Posting HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.company/deal/OXB-2026-1874 (I added the cost model as an attachment on the deal).

If this sounds good I can draft a narrow term sheet and route for review. Also, we can schedule a short call Friday to walk procurement through the DocuSign flow.

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Solutions Architecture
Redwood Inference

From: Aisha Gomez <aisha.gomez@oxbridge.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@oxbridge.ai>
Date: Sat, 14 Aug 2026 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated cluster sizing: floor, burst lanes, and staged-commit options (Oxbridge Therapeutics)

Karthik / Mina —

Appreciate the quick clarifications — that all reads well. We prefer Option 2 (Staggered Onramp) with a 12 GPU baseline, explicit weekday burst windows 08:00–18:00 PT, and pilot-conversion credits applied to month 1. Procurement will expect the DocuSign term with the 30-day pilot termination clause and the commitment smoothing schedule spelled out. 

Next: please send the DocuSign link and the term summary. We’ll aim to route internally next week and get final sign-off by Aug 26.

Best,
Aisha
Head of Platform Engineering
Oxbridge Therapeutics
